domain: A3 privacy and A6 store/consumer compliance (sweep a3, blind; baseline 8d9b98a2, HEAD 53b6df82, live site deployed from 72a4d1e4 with the game pinned to 257a766c)

risks.title: README says the hosted build is offline, but a playable build is live at /play/
risks.player_impact: Someone reading the public README, such as a parent checking for flashing risk, is told no build is hosted, while a flashing build is served at /play/ behind a gate and the holding page says the opposite.
risks.evidence: README.md:7 (committed, unchanged since 72a4d1e4) says 'The hosted build is offline for now'. A curl GET of /play/ returned 200 with the gated Godot page, index.wasm (38,450,604 bytes) and index.pck (9,034,688 bytes) were last modified 2026-11-05, and the pck holds build_info commit 257a766.

risks.title: The interim flashing build cannot be retired at its 2026-11-15 expiry by the normal path
risks.player_impact: The gated flashing build stays public after the owner's approved end date. The page's line 'may be taken down without notice' now relies on someone changing a GitHub setting by hand.
risks.evidence: The expiry is checked only when a new deploy runs: check-site-interim.mjs:78 fails that deploy and never removes the live site. Deploy needs every CI job (ci.yml:528), and CI has not run, so even tools/site-offline.mjs plus a push cannot change the site. A read-only gh api call shows Pages build_type 'workflow'.

risks.title: Civilian deaths are simulated, with no age rating, content descriptor or age gate anywhere
risks.player_impact: Before a store release, rating questionnaires need violence against civilians disclosed. Today neither the page nor the game tells players or parents about it, and nothing gates by age.
risks.evidence: collateral.gd:4 says every civilian death goes through kill() (line 294), with caps by tier. A grep of ui/data/*.json and the site notice files found no age, child or parental text. I did not check whether deaths are drawn on screen.
risks.needs_outside_expert: A ratings specialist for the IARC and Steam content surveys (and for regional boards if sold where they apply).

risks.title: The About page calls the engine 'official' 4.7.2-stable, but the served engine is a custom patched build
risks.player_impact: A small factual error in the licence notice. The licence texts themselves are complete.
risks.evidence: The live about page says 'Godot Engine 4.7.2-stable (official)'. The served index.wasm has SHA-512 ae2abcc2..., equal to the pinned custom template's wasmSha512 (web-template.json:15), and contains the string 'Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.custom_build'. The patch is published as a GitHub release asset.

risks.title: The public repo exposes the owner's Windows account name, local paths and a probable home LAN address
risks.player_impact: This is not player data. It weakens the pseudonymous owner's privacy: 52 committed files contain C:/Users/<account> paths, and a 10.x home address appears as a worked example.
risks.evidence: A git grep for 'Users/<account>' at HEAD matched 52 files. lan.gd:231 and lan_kit.mjs:3 use 10.0.0.135 as the host example. That address is private and not routable from outside the home network. Commit identities use a GitHub noreply address, which is fine.

risks.title: The privacy notices say nothing about on-device storage
risks.player_impact: The game keeps settings, tutorial flags and (at HEAD) up to 24 planet-cache files in the browser's IndexedDB or user://. None of it is personal, but 'collects and sends no personal data' is the only privacy statement.
risks.evidence: ui_prefs.gd writes user://ui_prefs.json (keys such as howto_seen, options and menu are set in ui_hud.gd). remap.gd writes user://input.json. field_cache is enabled with keep 24 (field.json:25-26). The live build 257a766c has ui_prefs but not field_cache.
risks.needs_outside_expert: EU/UK privacy counsel, on whether the strictly-necessary storage exemption covers this or a one-line disclosure is advisable before a store release.

risks.title: The Web export preset does not exclude net/ (LAN and ENet code), unlike the desktop presets
risks.player_impact: The next public web build will carry unused LAN networking code. It is not wired into the game, but it contradicts the stated rule that public builds exclude net/.
risks.evidence: Line 11 (Web) has no 'net/*' in exclude_filter; lines 55, 101 and 132 (desktop) do. Shipped render/ui/sim code mentions NetLan only in comments. The live pck has no net/ files, because net/ did not exist at 257a766c.

risks.title: Desktop presets lack store basics: unsigned Windows exe with blank publisher and version, macOS ad-hoc only and not notarized
risks.player_impact: A store or public desktop release would trigger OS 'unknown publisher' or Gatekeeper warnings and carry no copyright or version info.
risks.evidence: Windows has codesign/enable=false and empty file_version, product_version, company_name and copyright. macOS has codesign identity '' and notarization=0. No desktop build is published: the only unexpired Actions artifact is a web template, and no desktop-builds runs are listed.

checked_ok.area: Outbound network calls in shipped code
checked_ok.where: git grep at HEAD over sim/render/ui/audio/net (tools excluded); live index.js
checked_ok.why: No HTTPRequest, HTTPClient, WebSocket, WebRTC, fetch, sendBeacon, analytics, crash reporting or update check. The only sockets are LAN-only ENet in net/, which main code does not call. The live index.js fetch and XHR calls load only its own pck and wasm.

checked_ok.area: External resources on the live site
checked_ok.why: Every page loads only same-origin files (index.js, wasm, pck, icons, manifest) with inline CSS and JS. There are no fonts, CDNs or trackers, the pages are noindex, and no service worker is served (404).
head_include handles fullscreen, wake lock and key handling only. The audio snippet only resumes AudioContexts. Neither has a network call or storage.

checked_ok.where: tools/site.json (no crumbs key); tools/site-crumbs.mjs:1-3; live /play/ source
checked_ok.why: Crumbs are off, so the page has no localStorage use or cookie. Engine user:// uses IndexedDB only for game files.

The report holds coarse platform, browser family and major version, screen size, settings and the player's notes. The send target is 'none', so it only reaches the clipboard. The github/mailto options are off and show a review screen first.
The window title and --lan-log never include an IP, the failure text drops the address, and the host accepts only its own /24. The host IP appears only in the private kit's .cmd shortcuts.

checked_ok.area: Live claim: fight director is ordinary code, not an AI model
checked_ok.where: git grep for onnx/tflite/neural/llm/api keys, and model or binary files, at HEAD
checked_ok.why: No model files, GDExtensions or AI API calls ship. The opponent is tuned by data (data/director/ai.json). Gemini-suggested numbers are offline authoring, which the disclosure covers.

checked_ok.area: Live claims: beams gouge trenches, buildings break in stages, scars persist
checked_ok.where: sim/director/beam.gd:618-619; sim/world/structures.gd:98-100; sim/world/store.gd:14,22; same functions at 257a766c
checked_ok.why: Beams scorch grooves, buildings have stages 0-4, and the scar store refuses rather than evicts at MAX, keeping the deform write. No terrain healing was found. All of this is present in the live pinned build.

checked_ok.where: sim/core/wrap.gd:7,12; data/biomes/*.json (city, desert, ocean, mountain); data/combat/recipes.json:316
checked_ok.why: The world wraps, the four named biomes exist, and the moveset has a medium class next to light and heavy.

checked_ok.area: Live claims: 'a limited test build is up' and 'page collects and sends no personal data'
checked_ok.why: A gated playable build is served at /play/, unlinked from /. The holding page has no script or external resource.

checked_ok.area: Flash notice versus the live build's lock
checked_ok.where: live /play/ gate text; live pck 'lock_reduce_flashing': true; ui/data/options.json:45-46
checked_ok.why: The gate's statement that Reduce flashing is locked on matches the served pck. The README's 'Reduced motion' setting exists.

checked_ok.where: live /about/ (Godot MIT, OFL-1.1, full component list, FTL and others); ui/widgets/ui_licences.gd:5,19-27; ui/data/howto.json:96-112
checked_ok.why: The web build links its notices from the gate. The game shows engine-supplied licence text in-game, which covers desktop builds. No font files are bundled beyond the engine's own.
The AI-generated reference music and review images are excluded from export, and no music tracks are committed.
No child-directed copy and no data collection, so no children's-privacy obligations are triggered by the current builds.
Every listed path exists at HEAD.

limits: I did not run the game, Godot, Chrome or any capture, so runtime behaviour (what is drawn, what reaches IndexedDB, desktop engine log contents) is from code reading, not observation.
project.godot sets no logging option. I did not verify what the engine's default desktop file log records (likely GPU and OS names), and it stays local.
I did not verify the accuracy of the flash statement. The recorded full-set pass is for d3f1ca0e, not the live 257a766c, and flash measurement belongs to another domain.
My grep-based inspection of the live pck may miss strings inside compressed binary-token scripts (script_export_mode=2). File paths and JSON data were readable.
The private LAN and kept builds given to Orb and Orb 2 are not in the repo, so I judged them only from the kit scripts (net/tools/lan_kit.mjs, tools/preview/blackbox.mjs).
As instructed, I did not read docs/legal, docs/ep, docs/net, docs/qa, docs/production, docs/accessibility, homework or audit (apart from the named live-site-index.html).
